experiments.name: dependent chain
experiments.asm: vfrecip.s $vr0, $vr0; vfrecip.s $vr0, $vr0; vpickve2gr.w $r4, $vr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; vreplgr2vr.w $vr0, $r4
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 2000 --iters 300 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 1065353216; vreplgr2vr.w $vr0, $r4; li.d $r5, -1; li.d $r6, 0' --asm 'vfrecip.s $vr0, $vr0; vfrecip.s $vr0, $vr0; vpickve2gr.w $r4, $vr0, 0; and $r4, $r4, $r5; or $r4, $r4, $r6; vreplgr2vr.w $vr0, $r4'

latencies.notes: Data-dependent latency. Chain: tested op, then vpickve2gr.w+and+or+vreplgr2vr.w to restore the input pattern; the 7-cycle closure is subtracted (calibrated with vadd.b/xvadd.b). Swept 26 operand values including 0, powers of two, max, minnorm, maxsub, minsub, Inf and NaN: latency 11-29 cycles, CPI 6-15. The stored experiment uses 1.0. Measured on 2026-11-17 on LA464, core 0.

throughput.notes: Data-dependent throughput, 8 independent lanes. CPI ranges 6-15 over the same 26-value sweep; the stored experiment uses 1.0.

notes: Latency model, fitted and validated on this core with a two-copy chain (the stored experiment runs the operation twice, subtracts the 7-cycle closure and divides by 2). Classes: 11 cycles for special operands (0, Inf, NaN), 15 cycles for the exact / power-of-two path (the stored sample uses 1.0), 29 cycles for a general operand. For 32-bit lanes the vector latency equals 2 x the scalar latency - 5, because the 32-bit lanes make two passes over the 64-bit datapath and share the setup/rounding. 64-bit vector lanes match the scalar numbers exactly and run in parallel, only the slowest lane matters. Re-derived with the two-cycle cross-domain calibration: movfr2gr and movgr2fr are 2 cycles each, movgr2frh.w is 3, the flag pair is 7/15, vpickve2gr is 3, xvpickve2gr is 5, and vreplgr2vr/xvreplgr2vr are 2 (3 for the byte and half-word broadcast).
